requirements.evidence: All contract classes are present with the required signatures: CreateQueue (app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:22), UpdateQueue with named nullable params (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:22-28), SetQueueAccess (app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:24-29), the QueuePermission enum with only Call, the QueueAccess model (table, HasFactory, array cast, membership()/queue()), a factory that keeps membership and queue in one entity (database/factories/QueueAccessFactory.php:29-31), and QueuePolicy with create/update/manageAccess/call. Name is trimmed and checked for 1-255 chars, and the slug is slugified and must be unique per entity (ValidatesQueueAttributes.php:18-52). Race handling catches UniqueConstraintViolationException and turns it into a ValidationException (CreateQueue.php:36-37, UpdateQueue.php:54-55). There is no delete action. Revoke is logged only when $deleted > 0 (SetQueueAccess.php:51). CallNextTicket authorizes after the active check (CallNextTicket.php:32). Ticket::call runs lock, then inactive check, then authorize, then the LogicException (Ticket.php:96-124). The migration has cascading FKs and the unique pair. All three required docs and the CHANGELOG are updated.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes are in app/Actions, and each action authorizes inside itself through Gate::forUser(...)->authorize. The policy is the single source of truth. QueueAccess sets #[Fillable] deliberately. The migration has a timestamped generator-style name and a reversible down() (create_queue_access_table.php:28-31). docs/business-rules.md, docs/database-schema.md, docs/architecture.md and CHANGELOG are kept in sync, and PHPDoc is on the public methods. Small deviation: a new Concerns trait (app/Actions/Concerns/ValidatesQueueAttributes.php) adds a pattern that the 'one class per use case' guidance does not mention, although it is justified by sharing between two actions.

security.evidence: Every new action authorizes before it reads or writes (CreateQueue.php:24, UpdateQueue.php:29, SetQueueAccess.php:30). Cross-entity membership is rejected (SetQueueAccess.php:32-36). Permissions are checked against the enum with strict in_array and is_string (SetQueueAccess.php:81-87). The call path is closed on both CallNextTicket and Ticket::call, which removes the previous 'any member may call' hole. The policy denies non-array permission payloads. Mass assignment uses an explicit Fillable list. No UI is involved.

tests.evidence: New test files are CreateQueueTest, UpdateQueueTest, SetQueueAccessTest and QueuePolicyTest. They cover the happy paths for owner and admin, trimming and slugify, the 255/256-char limits, empty slugs, duplicate slugs within an entity versus across entities, simulated unique-index races (CreateQueueTest.php:86-104, UpdateQueueTest.php:78-96), and audit logs including the case where a revoke has nothing to delete. They also test invalid or non-string permissions, cross-entity membership, unauthorized actors including employee self-grant, corrupted permission payloads (QueuePolicyTest.php:76-87), and cascades. Call authorization is tested across every CallMode with four kinds of unauthorized caller (CallNextTicketTest.php:256-287), plus ordering for inactive-before-auth and auth-before-LogicException (IssueTicketTest.php:206-231). Existing tests were updated to use an authorized caller (managerOf) and were not weakened.

simplicity.evidence: The code is lean overall and reuses existing pieces: Validator, Str::slug, the Gate, lockForUpdate as used in sibling actions, and Eloquent upsert. The shared trait avoids duplication between CreateQueue and UpdateQueue. Minor extra code: the policy decodes JSON a second time because it assumes value() skips the cast (QueuePolicy.php:62-64).

readability.evidence: Methods are small and well named, with useful comments on lock ordering and upsert casts. One comment is inaccurate: QueuePolicy.php:62 says 'Query-builder value() bypasses the model cast', but Eloquent Builder::value() goes through the model, so the cast is applied. The test file defines a global helper `can()` (QueuePolicyTest.php:14), a generic name that could collide.

scope.evidence: Every change serves the task: actions, policy, model, factory, migration, docs and tests. The docs/architecture.md line edit (line 137) is doc sync for the new authorization boundary. The test helpers in tests/Pest.php are needed by the updated tests. No UI, delete action or extra permissions were added.

issues.explanation: The comment claims value() bypasses the array cast, but the Eloquent builder applies it. The extra json_decode is therefore unneeded and could even accept a double-encoded string such as "[\"call\"]" as a valid grant instead of denying it as corrupted.
It introduces a new Concerns trait pattern under app/Actions. This is reasonable for sharing between two actions, but the conventions do not describe it.
A global test helper named `can()` is generic and risks name collisions across test files.
The 'no delete action' test greps file names in app/Actions. It is brittle and checks little real behavior.

review.summary: The change adds CreateQueue, UpdateQueue and SetQueueAccess actions, the queue_access table, model and factory, the QueuePermission enum and a QueuePolicy, and it enforces the call ability in both CallNextTicket and Ticket::call in the required order. Docs and CHANGELOG are updated, and thorough tests cover authorization, validation, races, audit logging and corrupted data. Only small readability nits remain (a misleading cast comment that leads to a redundant re-decode), so I would approve with nits.
